source.title: Gradient Dynamics of Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks
source.authors: Francis Williams; Matthew Trager; Cláudio T. Silva; Daniele Panozzo; D. Zorin; Joan Bruna

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results on shallow univariate least-squares interpolation dynamics, but does not test the benchmark training-error, bad-minima, depth, initialization-speed, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern spline interpolation and neuron dynamics. It cites prior work on spurious minima and gradient descent convergence, but those cited findings are not its own results. Its reported figures and descriptions do not measure classification error or the outcomes named by V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study measures interpolation shape and neuron motion in shallow univariate ReLU regression. It does not measure any version's specified outcome. Initialization changes implicit bias here, but training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth are not tested. Spurious-minimum findings are cited from other studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with qualifications: the authors show that parameterization, normalization and initialization change interpolation bias in shallow univariate ReLU networks. Adaptive dynamics concentrate knots at selected samples; the idealized kernel regime yields curvature-minimizing interpolants, with cubic splines under appropriate initialization distributions. They establish no clear advantage of either regime in this setting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient flow or gradient descent for shallow univariate ReLU least-squares interpolation, rather than the benchmark classification, architectures, and outcomes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpolation dynamics depend on parameterization, normalization, initialization, and δ; the numerical experiment varies δ.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization, parameterization and width scaling determine whether shallow univariate ReLU regression produces adaptive linear-spline behavior or smooth kernel interpolation; conditional-uniform initialization yields cubic splines in the idealized random-feature limit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In shallow univariate ReLU least-squares regression, initialization and parameterization control interpolation bias and knot adaptation.

record.problems: The empirical setting is highly simplified: shallow networks, one-dimensional inputs, scalar outputs and least-squares interpolation. Several qualitative outcomes are conveyed through figures without numerical measurements or uncertainty estimates. The paper notes that its mean-field analysis does not easily extend to deeper architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed versions were reported. Cited results from other work were not extracted as this paper's own findings.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 convolutional-network training classification error, including random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts and the specified initialization or normalization alternatives.
Initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth through signal or gradient preservation, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature evolution, recovery and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate inability to assess V1–V6, not absence of the reported spline phenomena. Section 4's cubic-spline paragraph contains inconsistent δ signs; Sections 3.2–3.3 and the Figure 5 discussion consistently identify δ = −∞ with training only c.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons, identity shortcuts, batch normalization, and training error on ImageNet or CIFAR-10.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed comparisons, orthogonal initialization, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: shallow univariate ReLU network in canonical parameterization
rows.size_stated: m neurons; no specific width stated for this result
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow on least-squares interpolation in the canonical parameterization; the paper characterizes the active dynamics.
rows.measure: Qualitative interpolation behavior and neuron locations
rows.value: The dynamics favor piecewise-linear functions; neurons converge at certain sample points where the residual is large and of opposite sign from neighboring residuals.
rows.note: This is a result about univariate least-squares interpolation and adaptive knot placement, not classification error or any listed version.
rows.check: The qualitative finding is supported but measures no listed version. Qualify the convergence wording: Section 3.1 describes attraction or repulsion conditional on current residuals and a weighted average of other residuals, rather than unconditional convergence of all neurons to samples.

rows.subject: shallow univariate ReLU network in full parameters
rows.size_stated: m neurons; no specific width stated for this result
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow under kernel-regime initialization; the paper characterizes the kernel interpolation solution.

conditions.value: first-layer weights significantly larger than second-layer weights (δᵢ ≪ 0)

rows.baseline: active regime yields adaptive linear splines
rows.value: Kernel learning yields smooth cubic splines for the stated appropriate initial distributions; kernel learning has no adaptation to input data points.
rows.note: The paper specifies initialization and distribution assumptions for the spline result; this does not test training classification error.
rows.check: Interpolation shape measures no listed version. Theorem 5 concerns the idealized infinite-width random-feature limit with first-layer parameters fixed and outer weights initially near zero; exact cubic splines require the stated conditional-uniform initialization assumptions.

rows.check: Interpolation shape measures no listed version. Figure 5 specifies 10000 epochs, not 10000 neurons; width is not stated there. At δ = −∞ the experiment trains only c, rather than all parameters.
